chain.label: FAA/Marlin Air check-airman appointment failure
chain.trigger: the POI...did not seek further information regarding the nature or circumstances of the revocation...he assumed that the revocation was the result of a personal issue with prescription medications

chain.label: First officer inadequately trained/current in Citation
chain.trigger: the airplane records showed that the airplane was actually flown a total of 0.6 hour flight time during the flight training and checkride; ...The accident trip was the first officer's first revenue flight since Marlin Air rehired him

caused_by.evidence: the accident captain, acting in his role as FAA-designated check airman, administered the first officer's subsequent flight training and checkride

chain.label: Pilots skipped formal preflight/taxi checklist procedures
chain.trigger: the pilots discussed some tasks that were on preflight checklists but did not perform a formal challenge-response checklist procedure as they were leaving MKE

caused_by.evidence: the captain did not always adhere to company procedures or comply with regulations...routinely abbreviated checklists

chain.label: Autopilot/yaw damper buttons identical and confusable
chain.trigger: the yaw damper and autopilot engage buttons are identical in size, shape, type of operation...located adjacent to each other near the aft end of the cockpit center console, out of a pilot's normal field of vision

chain.label: Preexisting chafed/short-circuited wiring in first officer's control yoke
chain.trigger: sometime before the accident, at least two short circuits occurred in a bundle of wires in the first officer's control yoke/column...one of the short circuits occurred between the pitch trim power supply wire and the adjacent steel surface

chain.label: Abnormal flight control situation shortly after takeoff
chain.trigger: about 1557:51...the captain asked, 'why am I fighting the controls here?'

caused_by.evidence: anecdotal evidence indicates that inadvertent activation of the autopilot when attempting to engage the yaw damper is not an uncommon occurrence
This short circuit exposed the cores of multiple wires, providing a potential source of power to the pitch trim motor

chain.label: First officer's uncoordinated trim inputs during emergency
chain.trigger: about 1559:07, the first officer asked, 'how's that, any better?'...the NTSB's airplane performance study indicated that the airplane banked sharply after this statement

caused_by.evidence: it is likely that, at some time during the accident sequence, the first officer manipulated the aileron and/or rudder trim in an effort to help the captain with the control problems

the CVR evidence indicates that the pilots did not coordinate with each other regarding trim inputs, and it is likely that the first officer's trim inputs aggravated, rather than ameliorated, the situation

chain.label: Captain failed to reduce airspeed and prioritize aircraft control
chain.trigger: the captain allowed the airplane to accelerate and climb after takeoff...while he and the first officer tried to troubleshoot the control anomaly

caused_by.evidence: if the pilots had simply maintained a reduced airspeed while they responded to the situation, the aerodynamic forces on the airplane would not have increased significantly
the first officer's trim inputs aggravated...the situation

chain.label: Poor crew coordination throughout the emergency
chain.trigger: the first officer provided little help to, and likely hindered, the captain during his attempts to deal with the flight control anomalies during the accident flight

caused_by.evidence: as a result of the first officer's poor flying skills, his lack of airplane systems knowledge, and both pilots' lack of communication and coordination
as the emergency escalated, the captain began to take over the radio calls while he continued to handle the airplane and troubleshoot the control problem

chain.label: Final loss of control after captain transferred controls to first officer
chain.trigger: about 1600:36, the captain stated, 'you hold it, I'm gonna try to pull circuit breakers'...at 1600:40...'we're not...holding it'

caused_by.evidence: the captain instructed the first officer to take control of the airplane while he...tried to pull circuit breakers; performance data suggest that almost immediately after the first officer took control, the airplane rolled to the left and descended into the lake
the first officer provided little or no support to the captain...and was arguably a distraction

chain.label: Airplane impacted Lake Michigan
chain.trigger: physical evidence indicated that the airplane impacted Lake Michigan at a speed of about 243 knots, in a steep (about 42°) nose-down, left-wing-low attitude

caused_by.evidence: the airplane rolled to the left and descended into the lake

chain.label: Six fatalities, airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The two pilots and four passengers were killed, and the airplane was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: impacted Lake Michigan...The two pilots and four passengers were killed
